title: Human-reviewed duplicate-merge workflow (precision-first)
context: The Wikidata reconciliation pass (recon-001) produced a candidate-match worklist requiring human review. Conflating two different real people is both a data error and a privacy risk, so no merge ships without human confirmation. This task builds the workflow tooling — a review interface or structured worklist process — through which a reviewer confirms or rejects each candidate match, and implements the merge operation that combines both records' provenance and evidence while remaining reversible and auditable.
objective: Build a human-reviewed duplicate-merge workflow that allows a reviewer to confirm or reject each candidate Wikidata and within-corpus match from the recon-001 worklist, executes confirmed merges in a way that preserves all source provenance and evidence from both records, is reversible, and produces a dedup audit report showing zero confirmed false merges in the audit sample.
acceptanceCriteria: No automatic merge ships without human confirmation; each candidate must be explicitly accepted or rejected by a reviewer.
Blocking-key strategy documented and consistent with recon-001 (no ad-hoc merges outside the strategy).
Confirmed merges preserve all provenance and evidence from both source records; no data is silently discarded.
Merges are reversible: a merge can be undone and both original records restored without data loss.
Dedup audit sample drawn after merge: zero confirmed false merges (two different real people conflated) in the audit sample.
Each merge is logged with: reviewer identity, date, candidate IDs, decision (accepted/rejected), and rationale.
pnpm build && pnpm test && pnpm lint pass; workflow tooling committed via PR.
output: packages/reconciler/src/ (TypeScript/ESM merge workflow tooling) with tests, merge log schema, and dedup audit report template, committed via PR.
